meta.title: Korean — Stage A
meta.subtitle: The first 922 words — start here once you can read hangul
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Korean → English (see the word in hangul, recall its meaning) and English → Korean. Each word is ONE note with TWO cards, each scheduled on its own. 922 words from stage A, the first of the three stages of the National Institute of the Korean Language's vocabulary list for learners (2003), taking you to about 922 words in all. TOPIK, the proficiency test, publishes no word list; this one is the state's own, graded by when a learner should meet each word. 3 of the stage's 925 headwords are left out rather than glossed from nowhere: English Wiktionary has no entry for them, or none for the homograph the list means (그래、뛰다、남대문시장 …) — mostly transparent derivatives such as -되다 and -적 forms of words carded here. The words are in the list's own order of frequency, commonest first. — The front shows the word in hangul; where the list has two words spelled alike (눈 "eye" and 눈 "snow"), it also shows the hanja or the phrase the list gives to tell them apart (90 of these). The back gives the Revised Romanization, the pronunciation in hangul where it differs from the spelling, the hanja of a Sino-Korean word, the meanings, a verb's or adjective's polite, past and formal forms, one row per hanja with its meaning, its eumhun and other words of the list written with it, and a fold of sentences. 801 of the 922 words carry example sentences, up to three apiece: real sentences from Tatoeba where the word has one meaning in the list, else the usage examples Wiktionary gives under the sense the card teaches, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside each. — Word list: 한국어 학습용 어휘 목록 (Korean vocabulary list for learners), National Institute of the Korean Language, 2003, under the Korea Open Government Licence Type 1. Meanings, romanization, pronunciation, hanja, conjugated forms and the examples marked as Wiktionary's: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Hanja meanings: the Unicode Unihan database (Unicode License). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, found with the Kiwi morphological analyser.

fields.English:
noun
  1. thing; something; that which; what; used to designate any object, action, or phenomenon, forming noun phrases.
  2. an object belonging to an owner; forms constructions equivalent to English possessive pronouns. Colloquially pronounced 꺼 (kkeo) with initial tensing.
  3. Emphasizes the speaker's certainty about the preceding verb or adjective.
  4. Used as an element in a number of verbal suffixes; see the "Derived terms" section.
fields.Examples:
제 것입니다.
It's mine.
우스운 것 같네.
I think this is ridiculous.
나 울 것 같아.
I'm about to cry!

fields.English:
verb
  1. to do; used to vaguely refer to almost any action, in particular
  2. to prepare, to make (food, clothes, etc.)
  3. to make a certain facial expression
  4. to have, to eat
  5. to wear, to put on (accessories such as hats or jewelry)
fields.Examples:
뭐 해요?
What are you doing?
그만 해!
Stop it!
다시 해.
Start over.

fields.English:
verb
  1. to stay, remain in a location
  2. to keep working for a company
  3. to stay in a certain state
  4. for time to pass
  5. to be (in a state)
adjective
  1. to be (in a place); to exist
  2. to have
fields.Examples:
잘 있어!
Take care!
백 있어.
There are a hundred.
경단 있어?
Do you have some dango?

fields.English:
verb
  1. to become
  2. to come, to arrive
  3. to be permissible; to be OK; may
  4. to be... -ed; follows nouns and nominals to form passive verbs. The noun functions as the -이 (-i) / -가 (-ga)-complement of the verb. When there is no particle in between, the construction is written without spaces.
  5. Forms certain adjectives.
fields.Examples:
안 돼.
No, you can't do that.
안 돼!
No way!
왜 안돼?
Why not?

fields.English:
noun
way, means, possibility, ability; used to express ability, in constructions equivalent to the English modal "can"
fields.Examples:
그러는 수밖에 없겠네.
I suppose that's all you can do.
움직일 수가 없다.
I can't move.
중국을 갔을 수도 있어요.
He might have gone to China as well.

fields.English:
pronoun
I, me; the first-person singular plain (non-polite) pronoun
fields.Examples:
나 피나
I'm bleeding.
왜 나야?
Why me?
난 몰라.
Dunno.

fields.English:
determiner
that (of what has been already said or known)
pronoun
he, she
fields.Examples:
그 남자는 일본인입니까 아니면 중국인입니까? ― 그는 중국인입니다.

By the way, who is that girl?
그 사람들은 가족입니다.
Those people are family.

fields.English:
adjective
to have none; (to be) lacking; (to be) nonexistent
fields.Examples:
문제 없어!
No problem!
상관 없어!
It doesn't matter!
TV 없어?
Don't you have a TV?

fields.English:
adjective
auxiliary adjective used to negate the clause to which the main adjective belongs
verb
  1. used to negate the clause to which the main verb belongs
  2. to not do something
fields.Examples:
쉽지 않아.
It's not easy.
아프지 않아.
It doesn't hurt.
나쁘지 않네.
Not bad.

fields.English:
noun
  1. human being, person
  2. a person (encompassing both legal and natural persons)
fields.Examples:
너는 사람이야.
You're a person.
저 사람 알아?
Do you know that man?
나는 사람이다.
I'm a human.

fields.English:
pronoun
  1. we, us (refers to the speaker along with the listener(s), and possibly others, forming a collective “we”)
  2. we (refers to a group that includes the speaker and others of equal or lower status, but it explicitly excludes the person being addressed)
  3. my, our (prefixed to a noun to indicate that the noun is intimately associated with or belongs to the speaker’s group)
fields.Examples:
우린 이해해.
We understand.
우리는 안다.
We know.
우리가 졌다.
We lost.

이 그림을 본 적이 있다.
I have seen this picture.

왜 아니야?
Why not?
절대 아니야.
No way!
농담 아니야.
I'm not joking.

fields.English:
verb
  1. to see, to look at, to watch (to perceive with the eyes)
  2. to look after (a baby, child, house, etc.)
  3. to try, to examine (before the meal or purchase)
  4. to experience
  5. to try, to try out
adjective
  1. to seem (only in the present declarative conjugations)
  2. to intend to (only in the present declarative conjugations, often threat)
  3. to be out of fear that (only in the forms 봐 (bwa), 봐서 (bwaseo))
  4. to be given that (only in the form 보니 (boni))
fields.Examples:
영화를 보다
to watch a film
그들은 여러가지 화초를 보고 있다.
They are looking at various plants.
아이를 보다
to look after a child

그는 어렸을 때의 추억에 잠겼다.
He is reminiscing about his childhood memories.
그때의 나와 지금의 나는 다르다.
I am different now than I was at that time.
당연히 아무 때나 놀러 와도 되지!
Of course, you can come over any time!

fields.English:
noun
thing (alternative form of 것)
fields.Examples:
우는 거야?
Are you crying?
내 거예요.
It's mine.
넌 내 거야.
You're mine.

fields.English:
adjective
  1. the same
  2. like or similar (often used with 와 (wa)/과 (gwa))
  3. (to be) like; such as (indicates belonging to a similar group)
  4. look like; (to) resemble
  5. to be something that one can guess, predict
fields.Examples:
짭새들 같으니.
Fuck the police.
우스운 것 같네.
I think this is ridiculous.
나 울 것 같아.
I'm about to cry!

fields.English:
verb
  1. to give
  2. for someone; forms benefactive verbs.
fields.Examples:
앉아 줘.
Please sit.

Give me the money!
계속 해줘.
Please continue.

fields.English:
verb
  1. to go
  2. Marks a continuous action that either stretches from the present into the future, or involves physical movement away from the speaker.
  3. to appear
  4. to pass
  5. to last
fields.Examples:
잘 가!
Goodbye!
저리 가.
Beat it.
곧 갈게.
I'll be there soon.

fields.Hanja:
年
year; new-years
eumhun해 년

일년은 십이개월이다.

Listen to me carefully.

Where did you learn Japanese?

fields.English:
noun
  1. work (activity done for compensation or reward)
  2. a fact, an event, a situation (any kind of occurrence)
  3. deed (any human activity)
  4. urination, defecation, sexual intercourse

fields.English:
noun

fields.English:
verb
  1. to speak, to talk
  2. to explain (by talking)

그만 말해.

fields.English:
adverb
  1. but, however
  2. "like that, but;" contraction of 그러하나 (geureohana)

fields.English:
verb
  1. to come (to move towards the speaker)
  2. to fall
  3. Marks a continuous action that stretches from the past into the present.
fields.Examples:

fields.English:
verb
  1. to know, understand (to have information or knowledge about an object or situation through education, experience, thoughts, etc.)
  2. to know; realize (to realize or feel a fact or situation through awareness or senses.)
  3. to know; understand; appreciate (to realize or feel a psychological state in one's mind.)

fields.English:
noun
  1. sir or madam; Mr. or Ms.
  2. lineage; surname

fields.English:

fields.English:

  2. to be great
  3. to be loud
verb

  2. to grow up, to become an adult

fields.English:
noun
  1. day (twenty-four hours, a thirtieth of the month)
  2. short for 일요일(日曜日) (iryoil, “Sunday”)

fields.English:
adjective
many, much, a lot, plentiful

fields.English:
adjective
  1. to be good; great; excellent (excellent and satisfactory in features and content)
  2. to be good; nice (well-rounded and kind in personality)
  3. to be good; kind (kind and gentle in speech and act)
  4. to be good (above average in physical condition or health)
  5. to have a lot of nerve (not caring about saving face or being shameless)

Good day!

I'm good!

fields.English:
adverb
more, -er (to a greater extent)
fields.Examples:
더 크게.
Louder.

Faster.

fields.English:
verb
  1. to get, receive, take, obtain
  2. to endure, suffer (pain, hardship, etc.)
  3. to bathe in (the sunlight, moonlight, spotlight, etc.)
  4. to collect (fees), accept (applications, etc.)

fields.English:
pronoun
  1. that (thing near the listener)
  2. that (thing that has already been mentioned)

Come home.

verb
  1. to come out, come forth

  3. to be published, to be presented

adverb
